Staging (test builds): vault release log

Staging release 15 (test build)

Release 15 changes how your vault is recovered and unlocked, so that guesses at your PIN and password are counted where VettID cannot erase them.

Status

Status
Active
Published
2026-10-16
End date
Not set

The current release. New vaults are enrolled into it, and the app offers it to everyone on an older release.

Changes

  • New: to recover your vault on a new phone you enter your PIN and credential password together on one screen. You get ten attempts in total for that pair, not ten a day, and a wrong answer never says which of the two was wrong.
  • After two wrong attempts, each further one waits longer: 1, 2, 4, 8 and 16 days, then 30 days. On staging these waits are 10, 20, 40, 80 and 160 minutes. Changing your PIN or password gives you ten new attempts.
  • Every attempt is counted before it is tested, in a record that is locked for a day on staging (100 years in production). Each one is shown in History and sent to you by email.
  • A recovery cannot succeed until 72 hours after you last unlocked with both your PIN and password, so someone who starts one while you still use your phone has to wait for you to be absent.
  • Unlocking now also needs a secret that only your phone's hardware can produce, so your stored vault cannot be used to test PINs without your phone.
  • A new credential password needs at least 12 characters and must not be a common or easily guessed one.
  • VettID recovery is on by default for new vaults. Vaults from release 14 or earlier cannot move into release 15 and are set up again.
  • Needs app version 2.0.0-a1 or later.
  • Built from vettid-vault commit 2c3fe13 (tag release/staging/15) and independently rebuilt on 2026-10-16 with a matching PCR0.

Security

Security fix: update recommended

Before release 15, the limits on guessing a PIN and a credential password during a recovery were kept in data that VettID's hosts store, so a host that replayed stored data could have guessed faster than those limits allow. Release 15 keeps the count of attempts where the host cannot remove it and adds a secret from your phone to every unlock. We know of no use of this against any vault.
